The red-cheeked second-year reads out your time: five minutes. Shiv whistles, impressed.

memory.fact: Nala swam to the buoy and back in five minutes on a frosty dawn; Shiv said: I've created a monster.

event: Amara laughs about her beta plus, lightly, all the way down the tower stairs.
Eleven: the Foundations lecture; Amara's seat in front of yours is empty for the first half.
After, you go to the bathroom by the Long Room; someone is crying in the end cubicle, quietly.
You know the gold watch on the wrist resting on the cubicle door handle. "Amara?"

pictured.coverAfter: At the break you slip out to the bathroom along the corridor from the Long Room.

event: The crying stops. "Go away, Freckles," Amara says, thick-voiced. You sit on the floor outside.

memory.fact: Nala found Amara crying in a bathroom after her beta plus, and sat on the floor outside the cubicle.
Nala found Amara crying in a bathroom after her beta plus, and sat on the floor outside the cubicle.

event: "I do this," she says through the door. "After every test. Even when I win. Every single one."

memory.fact: Amara's confidence is practised; she cries in a bathroom after every test, however well she did.

event: You tell her she argued a room flat in four minutes last week; you saw it. A wet laugh.
"That's the trick," says Amara. "You make it look easy. Then you come in here."
She asks, through the door, what you do when you're frightened. You say: swim in a freezing mere.
"Mad," says Amara. "Utterly mad." But she's laughing properly now, and the bolt slides back.

memory.fact: Told Nala swims a freezing mere when frightened, Amara called it utterly mad, and laughed properly.

event: She comes out at last, eyes red, and fixes her face in the mirror, fast and expert, in silence.
"Keep this to yourself," she tells your reflection. "I'm good at that," you say.
Amara kisses your cheek, quick and fierce, smelling of cocoa butter. "Alpha minus. Damn you."

memory.fact: Amara asked Nala to keep her crying to herself; Nala said she's good at that; Amara kissed her cheek

event: Lunch: Amara sits with Priya and is dazzling and loud; she catches your eye once, and winks.
Two: practical; the cracked cups again; this time you breathe out longer, and your seam closes.
It closes all the way to the base, a faint line left; the demonstrator holds it to the light. "Yes."

memory.fact: Breathing out longer, Nala mended her cracked cup to the base, a faint line left; the tutor: Yes.

event: At the end bench Kit mends hers, back to the room; Amara, two benches down, watches Kit's back.
Amara looks at Kit's turned back a long moment, frowning, as if a sum won't come out.
Dusk in the empty Practice Hall; you sit on the front bench and look at Kit, openly, from the start.
Kit stands mid-floor, coat off, sleeves pushed up, and breathes out before she starts.
The sigil; the word; her hand stops in the air, and her face whitens. You hold her eyes. "Out."
She breathes out. The glim comes: small, wavering, then steadier, a pale bead of light. It holds.
You count aloud for her, softly: one, two, three, four, five. On six it goes out.
Kit lowers her hand slowly. "Five," she says. "Watched." Her voice shakes, and her eyes shine.
She does it twice more; the third time it holds to eight before it goes.

memory.fact: Watched by Nala in the dusk hall, Kit breathed out at her word and held a glim to five, then eight.
Watched by Nala in the dusk hall, Kit breathed out at her word and held a glim to five, then eight.

event: On the bench after, her head on your shoulder, Kit says: "Tomorrow, two pairs of eyes."
"Whose?" you ask. Kit is quiet a long time. "Bea's," she says. "She's decent. She said so."

memory.fact: Kit asked for two pairs of eyes tomorrow, Nala's and Bea's; Bea is decent, Kit said: she said so.

event: Room 1 is dark; it's Tuesday, one of Yusra's infirmary nights.
In 14 you take the essay out, and read the green question again under your lamp: whose wanting?
You think of Alan in the chair by the back window, and of this body, and can't say which.

memory.fact: Nala can't say whether her wanting is Alan's or this new body's, and leaves the question open.

event: You fall asleep with the essay on your chest and the question still open.
